title: Not yet examined
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the acute medical unit. Mr Kane, 45, has schizophrenia and was admitted six hours ago with shortness of breath. His notes say "known psychosis — approach with caution", and no doctor has yet examined him.

When you approach, he is calm and polite, but breathless.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Ask the psychiatry liaison team to see him before you examine him.
options.brief: Delays a medical assessment he needs now.
options.detailed: Liaison psychiatry may be helpful, but he needs a medical assessment for his breathlessness now.

options.text: Examine him yourself, explaining what you're doing as you go.
options.detailed: He has been breathless for six hours without a medical examination. He is calm, so there's no reason to delay, and explaining as you go helps him feel at ease.

options.text: Tell the nurse in charge and your registrar about the delay.
options.brief: A six-hour delay in assessment needs raising.
options.detailed: This delay needs to be known so his care can be prioritised and the team can understand how it happened.

options.text: Ask security to be present while you examine him.
options.brief: Unnecessary for a calm patient, and stigmatising.
options.detailed: Safety matters, but he is calm and polite. Bringing security would be unnecessary and could distress him.

options.text: Assume his breathlessness may be anxiety related to his illness.
options.detailed: Anxiety can cause breathlessness, but assuming it without examination risks missing a serious condition such as pneumonia or a pulmonary embolism.

options.text: Ask a nurse to do his observations and call you if they're abnormal.
options.brief: Observations alone aren't a medical assessment.
options.detailed: Observations are needed, but he also needs to be examined.

options.text: Remove the note from his record.
options.brief: You can't remove another clinician's entry.
options.detailed: The note may be unhelpful, but you can't delete it. You can raise it with the team and add your own observations.

options.text: Raise with the team how the note may have delayed his care.
options.brief: Labels can lead to unfair treatment.
options.detailed: The note may have led staff to avoid him. Raising this constructively helps prevent the same thing happening to other patients with mental illness.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you treat a patient with mental illness fairly, assessing his physical symptoms promptly and challenging a label that has delayed his care.
explanation.keyDetails: He has been breathless for six hours without examination. He is calm. A note in his record seems to have led staff to avoid him.
explanation.reasoning: [B] assesses him, [C] raises the delay, and [H] addresses the label. The distractors delay assessment ([A], [F]), stigmatise him ([D]), make a dangerous assumption ([E]), or alter the record ([G]).
explanation.competing: [A] is the hard distractor: liaison psychiatry can help, but his physical symptoms need assessing first.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, treating patients fairly and without prejudice.

references.title: Equality Act 2010
references.note: Fair treatment of people with mental illness.
